statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit. Excluded transaction submission, authenticated account interiors, video playback, search (robots-disallowed), and team microsites to avoid side effects and duplicate templates.

page.framework: Next.js/React plus multiple MLB shared web applications
page.notes: Large server-rendered sports/news/data portal with localized, subscription and authentication surfaces.

principleOutcomes.reason: No declared intent indicates MLB.com currently wants to expose transactional WebMCP/agentic tools; public content remains available as SSR HTML, so this emerging capability is treated as an opportunity rather than a failure. No user task in the audited news, scores, stats, subscription or localized surfaces requires on-device language-model or summarizer inference; absence is not a quality failure.

paths.description: Homepage: global navigation, score rail, lead news, consent, performance, privacy and memory baseline.
Scores listing: primary live-data task and responsive game cards.
Editorial article template including share metadata and newsletter form.
Spanish localized variant for lang, hreflang, locale and layout inspection.
MLB.TV subscription landing page for pricing, renewal, cancellation and commercial clarity.
Intentional unknown route for 404 and recovery behavior.
Authentication entry surface for modern-auth affordance inspection.

findings.summary: The main MLB homepage ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition probe reported colorScheme “normal” and body background rgb(245,245,245); the dark screenshot is visually identical to the default light surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark support at the root and use adaptive color tokens for page, card, text, and native-control surfaces.

findings.summary: Route and major state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS/HTML contained zero view-transition declarations, while route navigation is a hard document swap; the menu interaction video only shows local drawer behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance major route and state changes with same-document or cross-document View Transitions, while honoring reduced motion.

findings.summary: The cookie banner obscures primary content on first visit across key mobile templates.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots of home, standings, article, and subscription show a 250–300px consent panel covering roughly one third of the viewport and blocking content interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface with equally prominent accept/reject choices and keep settings available through a semantic dialog.

findings.summary: Promotional and navigation chrome displaces the primary homepage content.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the Ballpark Expedition banner, global navigation, and score rail consume about the first 270px before the lead story; the consent layer then covers the lower third.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or reduce promotional chrome on narrow screens so the lead story and task content dominate the first viewport.

findings.summary: Some controls and links are too small or too tightly spaced for touch.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size audit failed on the homepage even though the focused skip control had a visible box-shadow focus indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas and spacing to at least comfortable touch-target dimensions without removing visible keyboard focus.

findings.summary: Primary pages load far too slowly under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Homepage Lighthouse performance was 0.28 with LCP 32.1s, FCP 6.7s, TBT 1,730ms, and TTI 75.3s; article performance was 0.35 with LCP 21.8s. The raw trace independently measured LCP 17.6s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the true LCP resource, cut render-blocking dependencies, and delay nonessential personalization, ads, analytics, and media until after useful content.

findings.summary: Heavy JavaScript blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace found 7 long tasks, a 451ms longest task, and 649ms TBT; mobile layout observation also captured a 1,516ms task. Lighthouse measured 1,730ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile long animation frames, split long tasks, and schedule or defer noncritical hydration, ad, and analytics work.

findings.summary: The homepage ships an excessive request and byte load before core content settles.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 505 requests and 15.24MB transferred: 7.13MB script, 6.92MB images, 128 scripts, 205 images, and multiple parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route-level performance budget, consolidate critical CSS, defer third parties, and reduce initial JS/image delivery.

findings.summary: Key templates contain broken ARIA relationships and missing image alternatives.
findings.evidence: Homepage Lighthouse found prohibited aria-labelledby on tab panels, unnamed links/images and label/name mismatches; article Lighthouse found invalid aria-setsize and multiple content images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair tab/list semantics and provide meaningful alt text or explicit presentation roles for decorative images.

findings.summary: Small score, signup, and consent text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured homepage team records at 3.54:1 and article signup text at 2.87:1; consent links measured 4.01:1, all below 4.5:1 for this text size.
findings.suggestedFix: Use darker text/brand tokens and test all score, signup, and consent states to at least WCAG AA contrast.

findings.summary: Heading and ARIA structure is inconsistent across templates.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found no h1 and starts at h2; article Lighthouse failed heading order and list semantics, while homepage tab panels use aria-labelledby without a valid role.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every template one descriptive h1, preserve sequential headings, and implement complete tab/list patterns.

findings.summary: The article viewport restricts user scaling.
findings.evidence: Article Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because user-scalable=no or maximum-scale below 5 was present; the homepage also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and restrictive maximum-scale values, then verify reflow and target size at 200–400% zoom.

findings.summary: Homepage and article loads emit application, network, CORS, MIME, and hydration errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured failed login checks and CORS/MIME errors on home, plus invalid-date and React hydration errors #418/#423/#425 on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix hydration/date defects and isolate third-party failures so expected network denials do not produce uncaught errors.

findings.summary: Image dimensions and aspect ratios are unreliable.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 31 of 100 images without dimensions and 70 oversized; Lighthouse separately failed incorrect aspect ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit numeric width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and use correctly sized responsive variants.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and BFCache blockers remain in first- and third-party code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported unload listeners, deprecated Shared Storage/Topics usage, inspector issues, and BFCache failure reasons on both home and article.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload listeners, update or remove deprecated vendor integrations, and resolve BFCache and inspector blockers.

findings.summary: The audited news article has social tags but no structured article data.
findings.evidence: The article is a rich editorial entity; rendered probes/Lighthouse showed Open Graph metadata but no application/ld+json block.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate NewsArticle/Article JSON-LD matching the visible headline, author, dates, image, publisher, and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Security policy and cookie configuration are weak despite HTTPS.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP and no Permissions-Policy; cookie audit found all 52 observed cookies flagged insecure, with many SameSite=None and several roughly 390–400 days old.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a report-only then enforced CSP, add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest suitable SameSite and lifetime.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party collection begin before meaningful consent and dominate the page.
findings.evidence: Trackers primitive saw 80 third-party origins and 17 known tracker hosts; HAR attributed 495/505 requests and 15.01MB to third-party origins. Cookie screenshots still show the undecided consent banner while this traffic and 52 cookies were observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Block nonessential tags until consent, remove redundant vendors, batch essential analytics, shorten identifiers, and enforce a third-party request/byte budget.

findings.summary: The entry sign-in experience exposes no passkey option.
findings.evidence: The login entry screenshot shows an email-only first step and no passkey/WebAuthn affordance; no permission prompt appeared on audited page loads.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer discoverable passkey sign-in/conditional UI alongside recovery-compatible fallback authentication.

findings.summary: The localized site relies overwhelmingly on physical-direction CSS.
findings.evidence: Spanish content correctly uses lang=es and en/es hreflang, but stylesheet inspection counted 429 physical left/right declarations and only 4 logical-property declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace reusable layout spacing and positioning with inline/block logical properties and verify an RTL test locale.

findings.summary: The article newsletter form accepts an empty submission without a visible field error.
findings.evidence: Both email inputs lacked required and autocomplete; submitting empty produced no :invalid controls and no form error alert.
findings.suggestedFix: Make intent explicit, validate after interaction, show a clear inline error, set aria-invalid, and announce errors in a dedicated live region.

findings.summary: Many images are materially oversized for their rendered slots.
findings.evidence: The image primitive marked 70 of 100 homepage images oversized; HAR transferred 6.92MB across 205 image requests despite modern formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate tighter responsive breakpoints, retain srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, and avoid fetching offscreen variants before needed.

findings.summary: The homepage has a very large steady-state heap footprint.
findings.evidence: After GC, the baseline heap summary contained 2,578,233 nodes and 159.7MB self size; the repeated-menu run contained 2,587,441 nodes and 163.7MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the largest native/code/object populations, reduce initialized widgets and vendor runtimes, and lazy-mount below-fold modules.

taskList.title: Gate and consolidate third-party tracking until explicit consent
Cut initial route JS, image, request and main-thread budgets
Prioritize the LCP resource and remove blocking delivery chains
Repair accessible names, ARIA structure, headings, contrast and zoom
Deploy CSP, Permissions-Policy and secure cookie defaults
Make consent compact, balanced and non-obscuring
Fix hydration/runtime errors, deprecations and BFCache blockers
Add dimensions and right-sized responsive image variants
Add article JSON-LD and improve localized logical layout
Add humane newsletter validation/autofill and passkey entry

checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark emulation left color-scheme normal and body light; screenshot did not retint.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() returned no active animations and no reduced-motion CSS was needed for the settled state.
Forced-colors screenshot retained visible navigation, score text, controls and consent actions; focused skip control had a dual-ring box shadow.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered CSS feature inspection and transition video
checkOutcomes.evidence: No view-transition usage was found in rendered source; route changes remain document swaps.
No parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal interaction was observed on the representative templates, so there is no scroll animation implementation to assess.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal interaction was observed on the representative templates, so there is no scroll animation implementation to assess.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS feature inspection plus mobile screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Rendered CSS contains scroll-snap and overscroll-behavior, and horizontal score navigation retains native scrolling controls.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile screenshot and rendered CSS inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: On the long homepage, static promotional/nav/score chrome consumes substantial initial space and no scroll-state query was found.
No tooltip or edge-sensitive anchored popover was present in the representative first-load and primary-flow states; the main overlay is a modal consent surface.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip or edge-sensitive anchored popover was present in the representative first-load and primary-flow states; the main overlay is a modal consent surface.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Active section labels, score controls, article hierarchy, and subscription plan toggle provide clear directional and current-state cues.
Consent overlays obscure roughly one third of multiple mobile first viewports.
The consent implementation exposes DIALOG and role=dialog/aria-modal surfaces with visible close/settings controls.
Promotional banner, global nav and score rail delay the lead content on narrow home view.
All five tested content templates reported scrollWidth=clientWidth=360, viewport meta present, and zero horizontal overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered CSS inspection and mobile screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Rendered CSS contained @container/container-type usage and components visibly reorganized into narrow cards/tables.

checkOutcomes.method: Focus computed-style probe plus Lighthouse target-size audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Visible keyboard focus is present, but Lighthouse target-size failed on the homepage.
Scores/news purpose is clear, but first-visit consent obscures the next useful content/action on primary mobile templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative journey walkthrough without transaction side effects
checkOutcomes.evidence: Scores expose preview/tickets/story actions, the article content renders, and subscription pricing/BUY NOW/cancellation terms are visible without dead ends before purchase.
The deliberate invalid route renders a clear 404 heading, retry guidance and Customer Support link rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse mobile audits and DevTools trace summary
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse home LCP 32.1s/FCP 6.7s/TBT 1.73s and article LCP 21.8s; trace LCP 17.6s.
Observed CLS remained below 0.1 on all five templates: home 0.077, article 0.040, stats 0.019, standings 0.017, scores 0.001.
Trace found seven long tasks and 649ms TBT; layout observer caught a 1,516ms homepage task.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against rendered DOM resource structure
checkOutcomes.evidence: 505 requests/15.24MB with multiple parser-inserted VeryHigh styles and large script/image chains.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR resource totals plus Lighthouse diagnostics
checkOutcomes.evidence: 128 scripts transferred 7.13MB and Lighthouse reported unused JS/CSS opportunities.
Lighthouse found invalid ARIA, unnamed links/images, label-name mismatch and article images without alt.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit with node-level ratios
checkOutcomes.evidence: Measured failures include 3.54:1 score records, 2.87:1 signup text and 4.01:1 consent links.

checkOutcomes.method: Heading/landmark probe and Lighthouse structural audits
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage has no h1; article heading/list audits failed; tab panels have prohibited ARIA.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual text review plus mobile layout metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative mobile screenshots show readable line lengths, unclipped headlines and clear data alignment; no horizontal overflow was measured.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse viewport/target audits plus layout metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: Article restricts user scaling and homepage has undersized targets; mobile layout itself reflows without horizontal overflow.
Console contains login, CORS, MIME, invalid-date and React hydration errors.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM document probe, image primitive and Lighthouse asset audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Doctype/UTF-8 are valid, but 31 images lack dimensions, 70 are oversized and aspect-ratio audit failed.
Deprecated unload/Topics/Shared Storage APIs, BFCache blockers and inspector issues were reported.
All discoverability captures reported title and meta description present in raw HTML; home metadata is descriptive.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse SEO/viewport audits plus robots and DOM probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: Links are real hrefs and robots permits audited routes, but article viewport prevents normal scaling and Lighthouse found non-descriptive link text.

checkOutcomes.method: HTTP/raw HTML/DOM metadata and robots/sitemap inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Audited routes returned 200, canonical metadata exists, robots permits them, sitemap declarations are published, and en/es hreflang is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered metadata probe and Lighthouse SEO review
checkOutcomes.evidence: The editorial article has Open Graph metadata but no JSON-LD Article/NewsArticle block.
HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff/frame protection are present, but CSP and Permissions-Policy are absent and 52 cookies were flagged insecure.

checkOutcomes.method: Tracker, HAR, cookie and first-load visual evidence
checkOutcomes.evidence: 80 third-party origins, 17 known tracker hosts, 495 third-party requests and 15.01MB third-party transfer occurred during undecided consent.

checkOutcomes.method: First-load observation and login entry screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: No permission prompt fired on load, but the login entry offers email continuation without a passkey option.
HSTS and X-Frame-Options exist, but CSP/frame-ancestors via CSP and Permissions-Policy are absent; Referrer-Policy is only no-referrer-when-downgrade.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability raw-vs-rendered comparison and crawler screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: All five raw responses contain meaningful content and are not JS shells; no-JS coverage ranged 46–80%, including article text and standings/scores data.
The consent overlay blocks content and runtime logs include hydration/date/login failures, reducing robustness.

MLB.com is a live scores/news/streaming service whose core value depends on current network data; no project intent declares the website itself an offline installable app, and a separate official app is promoted.

checkOutcomes.method: Localized rendered-content and subscription state probe

Newsletter email controls have an accessible aria-label but no autocomplete token and are not marked required.

checkOutcomes.method: Subscription surface visual and text walkthrough without purchase

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline and post-interaction heap summary comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: After 10 menu open/close cycles, GC-normalized heap changed from 159.7MB/2,578,233 nodes to 163.7MB/2,587,441 nodes; top constructors remained broadly stable, with no clear unbounded interaction leak in this bounded run.

checkOutcomes.method: Single-state heap summary and constructor distribution
checkOutcomes.evidence: GC-normalized baseline is 159.7MB self size with 2.58M nodes, disproportionate for a content homepage.
No Detached* constructor entered the top retained constructor list after repeated menu interaction; Promise/Map/Set populations remained near baseline.
